previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia and other bypass-related issues was admitted to the surgery service for planned gastric bypass reversal. She underwent laparoscopic bypass reversal without intraoperative adverse events, recovered with initial NPO status and gastrostomy tube to gravity for decompression, and had a postoperative upper GI study showing no leak or obstruction. Pain control progressed from epidural to PCA and then to oral hydromorphone once she tolerated diet; her G-tube was clamped on postoperative day 3 and her diet was advanced sequentially to a Stage III diet with close monitoring of blood glucose, intake, and output. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable without evidence of infection or bleeding, ambulated independently, and was discharged home with instructions on Stage III diet, wound care with staples to be removed at follow-up, avoidance of NSAIDs, crushed pills, glucose monitoring with PRN glucose gel for hypoglycemia, and appropriate medications for pain, nausea, reflux prophylaxis, and constipation prevention.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient contacted the clinic due to nausea and inability to 
tolerate POs. She was admitted for IVF and symptom management. 

Neuro: The patient was alert and oriented throughout 
hospitalization. Pain was very well controlled. 
CV: The patient remained stable from a cardiovascular 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored.  
Pulmonary: The patient remained stable from a pulmonary 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored. Ambulation was 
encouraged throughout hospitalization.  
GI/GU/FEN: The patient was initially on a Bariatric Stage 3 
diet. Patient associated nausea with intake of protein shakes, 
advanced diet to mechanical soft. She was tolerating broth, 
cream of wheat and water without nausea. Patient received 
education on mechanical soft diet and encourage to get protein 
in diet.
ID: The patient's fever curves were closely watched for signs of 
infection, of which there were none.  
HEME: The patient's blood counts were closely watched for signs 
of bleeding, of which there were none.  
Prophylaxis: The patient received subcutaneous heparin during 
this stay and was encouraged to get up and ambulate.  

At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
and hemodynamically stable. The patient was tolerating a 
bariatric stage 3 diet, ambulating, voiding without assistance, 
and pain was well controlled. The patient received discharge 
teaching and follow-up instructions with understanding 
verbalized and agreement with the discharge plan.

Mental Status: Clear and coherent.

Discharge Instructions:
Please call your surgeon or return to the emergency department 
if you develop a fever greater than 101.5, chest pain, shortness 
of breath, severe abdominal pain, pain unrelieved by your pain 
medication, severe nausea or vomiting, severe abdominal 
bloating, inability to eat or drink, foul smelling or colorful 
drainage from your incisions, redness or swelling around your 
incisions, or any other symptoms which are concerning to you.  

Diet: Stay on Stage 4, soft mechanical diet until your follow up 
appointment. Do not self advance diet, do not drink out of a 
straw or chew gum  
Resume your home medications, CRUSH ALL PILLS.  

You will be starting some new medications:  
1. You are being prescribed Compazine, an anti-nausea 
medication. You can alternate this medication with Zofran, as 
needed with nausea.
2. You must not use NSAIDS (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory  
drugs) Examples are Ibuprofen, Motrin, Aleve, Nuprin and  
Naproxen. These agents will cause bleeding and ulcers in your  
digestive system.  

Activity:  
No heavy lifting of items ___ pounds for 6 weeks. You may  
resume moderate exercise at your discretion, no abdominal  
exercises.  

Wound Care:  
You may shower, no tub baths or swimming.  
If there is clear drainage from your incisions, cover with  
clean, dry gauze.  

Please call the doctor if you have increased pain, swelling,  
redness, or drainage from the incision sites.
